name: PhyX
intro: PhyX 是面向真实视觉场景物理推理的大规模基准。论文从 3,300 个候选问题经三级清洗得到 3,000 个独立问题，覆盖 6 个物理领域、25 个子领域和 6 种推理类型；每题配对开放题与选择题，并提供 Full-Text、Text-DeRedundancy、Text-Minimal 三种视图，形成 18,000 个核心评测实例。
org: The University of Hong Kong, University of Michigan, Independent Researchers, University of Toronto, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University
build_method: STEM研究生从允许再发布的多种来源采集, OE/MC双题型配对, 三文本视图与GPT-4o图像描述, 词汇重复检测/物理博士人工复核/最短10%过滤
metric: Accuracy（开放题由DeepSeek-V3判断等价；选择题先匹配选项字母，失败后回退同一Judge）
task_type: 多模态问答, 物理推理
eval_feature: 3,300到3,000筛选, 18,000核心实例, 1,000题testmini, 规则抽取与DeepSeek-V3 Judge
scale: 3,300个候选问题, 3,000个独立问题, 6,000个OE/MC问题, 18,000个核心实例, 1,000题testmini（6,000实例）
build_method_en: STEM-graduate expert collection from redistribution-compatible sources, paired OE/MC conversion, three text views and GPT-4o captions, then lexical duplicate detection, physics-PhD review, and shortest-10-percent filtering
eval_feature_en: 3,300-to-3,000 curation, 18,000 core instances, 1,000-problem testmini, rule extraction and DeepSeek-V3 judging
intro_en: PhyX is a large-scale benchmark for physics-grounded reasoning in realistic visual scenarios. The paper cleans 3,300 candidates into 3,000 unique problems across 6 physics domains, 25 subdomains, and six reasoning types. Every problem has paired OE and MC formats plus Full-Text, Text-DeRedundancy, and Text-Minimal views, yielding 18,000 core evaluation instances.
scale_en: 3,300 candidates, 3,000 unique problems, 6,000 paired OE/MC questions, 18,000 core instances, 1,000-problem testmini with 6,000 instances
metric_en: Accuracy; OE uses DeepSeek-V3 equivalence judging, while MC first matches the option letter and falls back to the same judge

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-22; review_scope=paper-aligned bilingual source-stage reconstruction; status=paper/source/geometry reviewed, formal publication assets intentionally not overwritten. Primary paper evidence is the latest arXiv record https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15929v2 and PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.15929v2. The downloaded v2 PDF SHA256 is fc4a3a5a69d6109b6dd215a7453f7a0166c286fa57f7fe167c51080bd54700e0. The official project page is https://phyx-bench.github.io/; its reviewed HTML snapshot SHA256 is 1e9652dcde3246e6d9ad2f2d8203caf78daf5a5eae1ba36030344ba0cf337387. The official implementation is fixed at https://github.com/NastyMarcus/PhyX/tree/2cee68b17643dc66feaa10406e93d708d99243fe. At that commit, README.md SHA256 is d63547d3fccb12c48b4b6e4492578a5cb12b48d8a67fb835a3cec287d48d9414, vlmeval/dataset/utils/phyx.py SHA256 is 3994c9615bcf26679d0488e32a13b607b7c50ae900873d233b290f5b02f8d148, dataset/md5.txt SHA256 is 5f7bebc0cddf1b594db6bdd44ef6ae0f6e862c2023f08acadaed50e5d577eba5, and LICENSE SHA256 is 15d4f980434dfb77361758be1460f936f2b3eaf0ce6d9f59feb74c32dec053c5. The Hugging Face release is fixed at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Cloudriver/PhyX/tree/5a23a2762d0626b5f319bd725138cc9b18b45d8f; its README.md SHA256 is 5a72326b93922bd85dddd1d5a314b7f0804f9519f1090ba49c97b346202f0abd. Construction evidence comes from paper section 2.2 and Appendix F. The authors first survey core physics disciplines and define six domains, 25 subdomains, and six physical-reasoning types. The domains are mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, wave/acoustics, optics, and modern physics. The six reasoning types are physical-model grounding, spatial-relation reasoning, multi-formula reasoning, implicit-condition reasoning, numerical reasoning, and predictive reasoning. STEM graduate students serve as expert annotators. Appendix F requires English questions, one realistic physical image per question, unambiguous short or option-checkable answers, complete structured fields, cross-checking between annotators, periodic random review, and team discussion for ambiguous entries. Sources include freely accessible online resources, textbooks, and other materials, and annotators are asked to use a wide range rather than a single source. Copyright-restricted material must be excluded, privacy-sensitive content avoided, and contamination risk reduced by avoiding simple questions whose answers are immediately available beside the prompt. Every OE item is converted to MC and every MC item to OE; MC items have four options with one correct answer. Every problem receives three parallel views: the original Full-Text, Text-DeRedundancy with image-duplicated prose removed, and Text-Minimal with only the core question. GPT-4o produces a fine-grained, self-contained image caption so text-only LLMs can be evaluated. These stages yield 3,300 candidates from various sources. Quality control is drawn with the paper's ordering: lexical-overlap detection flags potential duplicates; physics PhD students manually confirm and remove duplicates, validate scientific accuracy, and address dataset bias; then the shortest 10 percent by textual length are removed. The final benchmark has 3,000 unique images/problems, 3,000 OE plus 3,000 MC questions, and 18,000 core combinations across the two formats and three text views. testmini is a proportional random sample across the six domains containing 1,000 problems and 6,000 core instances. Evaluation evidence comes from sections 3.1-3.2 and Appendix D. The paper evaluates testmini using a universal three-step protocol. Step 1 generates a prediction from the selected image/caption, text view, and question format with the disclosed zero-shot instruction 'Please answer the question with step by step reasoning.' Step 2 applies disclosed rule-based extraction: the appendix shows boxed-answer handling and final-answer/correct-answer regex logic for OE, and option-letter A-D extraction for MC. Step 3 uses an LLM such as DeepSeek-V3 for semantic equivalence on OE. The paper explicitly says the judge is called multiple times and the answer is accepted only if the LLM succeeds in all attempts; a 200-example study reports more than 99 percent judge accuracy. MC first attempts direct option-letter matching; when that fails it reuses the OE judge template. The benchmark metric is binary Accuracy, reported across OE/MC, Full-Text/Text-DeRedundancy/Text-Minimal, domains, and reasoning types; no partial-credit metric was added. Prompt provenance is not guessed: Appendix D publicly discloses the CoT instruction, parser snippets, and figures for the answer judge, caption generation, and reasoning-type labeling. The current repository additionally releases few-shot judge prompt construction in phyx.py. Release drift is kept outside the paper flow. The Git repository contains 12 files per full/testmini subset across OE/MC, three text views, and image-versus-caption inputs. The pinned HF card exposes default 3,000/1,000 splits, four default-setting TSV files, and later multilingual and with-steps configurations; those later configurations are release extensions, not stages claimed by paper v2. A material evaluator drift is also explicit: the paper requires all attempts to agree positively, but the current released evaluator at 2cee68b17643 uses five retries with temperatures 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 and returns the first parseable 1/0 verdict. Therefore the current released evaluator's first parseable result is not represented as the paper's all-attempt consensus. The main pipeline follows the paper, while a dashed boundary records this implementation difference. The Git repository and HF card declare MIT, but that does not erase upstream copyright, licensing, redistribution, privacy, or fair-use constraints attached to collected source material. No system prompt, generation parameter, judge parameter, or parser behavior was invented beyond the pinned paper and released code. EN/ZH specs use identical node IDs, semantic types, sizes, positions, waypoints, edge types, and dashed secondary styles; English labels contain no Chinese, Chinese labels preserve the same claims, and the source-stage test locks line widths and topology.
